title: What is air pressure and why don't we feel it?
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why aren't we crushed by the air?
Why do my ears pop on a plane?
What does high pressure mean for the weather?

explain.say: Air may feel like nothing, but it has weight. The whole atmosphere above you presses with a force of about 10 tonnes on every square metre at sea level.

draw.text: What is air pressure and why don't we feel it?

explain.say: Air pushes not just down but in every direction at once: up, down and sideways. That push is called air pressure.

We don't feel squashed because the air and fluids inside our bodies push back outward just as hard, so the forces balance. You notice it only when pressure changes quickly, like ears popping in a plane.
Air pressure also shapes the weather. High pressure has sinking air and usually brings calm, dry weather, while low pressure has rising air and usually brings clouds, wind and rain.

faq.q: Why don't we feel air pressure?
faq.a: The air presses on us from all sides, and the air and fluids inside our bodies push back outward just as hard. With the forces balanced, we feel nothing.
asks: Why aren't we crushed by the air?

faq.q: Why do my ears pop on a plane?
faq.a: As the plane climbs, outside air pressure drops while the air behind your eardrum stays at the old pressure. When a small tube to your throat opens and lets the pressures even out, your ears pop.
asks: Why do ears hurt when flying?

faq.q: What do high and low pressure mean for the weather?
faq.a: High pressure has sinking air, which warms and dries, so it usually brings calm, clear weather. Low pressure has rising air that cools and forms clouds, so it often brings wind and rain.
asks: What does a falling barometer mean?

faq.a: With a barometer. Forecasters measure pressure in hectopascals, also called millibars; average sea level pressure is about 1013 hectopascals.

faq.q: Does air pressure change with height?
faq.a: Yes. Higher up there is less air above you pressing down, so pressure falls. At the top of Mount Everest it is only about a third of sea level pressure.
asks: Is there less air on mountains?

facts: Average sea level air pressure is about 1013 hectopascals, roughly 10 tonnes of force on each square metre.
Evangelista Torricelli invented the mercury barometer in 1643.

quiz.say: Why aren't we crushed by the weight of the air above us?
quiz.show: We are not crushed by air pressure because…

options.show: The fluids inside our bodies push back just as hard
options.say: The fluids inside our bodies push back just as hard

options.show: Our skin is too strong to dent
options.say: Our skin is too strong to dent

quiz.why: Air presses on us from every side, and the pressure inside our bodies balances it, so there is no overall squeeze.

wrong.0: Air does have weight: a column of it presses about 10 tonnes on every square metre.
wrong.2: Skin alone could not resist that pressure; the balance comes from the pressure inside us.
